issues.situation: In the bench rosters the 2x gate is not a 'nearly dead' test. A full 5-model Custodian Guard or Allarus unit gets the engine estimate 13.9 melee damage (bench logs print 'expected 13.9 melee dmg vs 6 HP'). That trips the gate at FULL health on a lone Blade Champion (6 W, 2.3x) and on Prosecutors (4 W, 2.9x). In the asym fixture it also trips on full Stormboyz (13.9 vs 6), Warbikers A/B (23.1 vs 10), Deffkilla Wartrikes (23.1 vs 9) and the Mek (27.8 vs 4). The Stompa trips it on Blade Champions, Wartrikes, Warbikers A/B and the Mek. CT-OVERKILL cuts a full Blade Champion's ch_damage from 27.8 to 12. CT-COMBO removes it from every multi-target declaration. I checked two bench-roster Custodes-mirror game logs on this machine, both with the base AI: ~/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/40k/logs/debug_20261031_035115.log and debug_20261031_035826.log. In them, 19 of 55 declarations involve such a target. 6 are gated single-target charges. 13 are multi-target declarations that list a Blade Champion or Prosecutors, e.g. 'Custodian Guard Epsilon declares a charge at Blade Champion Beta + Blade Champion Gamma + Prosecutors'. CT-COMBO rewrites these whenever the charger is at full strength. The evidence for the design is one custodes_lions position (3-model units, 7-W Blade Champions) where the gated target had 2 of 6 W left. No measured position covers full-health gated targets. The designer played only 1 Custodes-mirror pair (E -6.0, n=1) and no asym or Orks pair. A second effect: the gate turns on or off when the charger goes from 5 models to 4 (13.9 vs 11.1 dmg against 6 W), so the same target's value jumps by about 16 points before multipliers.
issues.proposed_change: Gate both arms on depletion as well as the ratio. Apply CT-OVERKILL and CT-COMBO only when the target has lost at least half its starting wounds: ct_hp <= 0.5 x the sum of the Wounds characteristic over all its models, dead ones included. Keep the 2x ratio too. The finding still flips (its target has 2 of 6 W left). Full-health characters and small units keep today's value, and the 4-vs-5-model boundary flip goes away. Then re-measure bench reach on all 3 fixtures as changed declarations per game, not as log lines.

issues.situation: The cap is blind to kill cards, and that likely breaks the brief's guard position s7431 r3. In measured play the gate mostly picks out lone CHARACTERs: 13 of the 14 measured single-target charges that trip it are at CHARACTERs (Mek x4, Beastboss x3, Blade Champion x2, Zodgrod, Snikrot, Logan, Chaplain). Charging them was on average slightly better than not charging (mean E -0.89, sd 2.63; 12 neutral, 1 harmful, 1 clear). The 11e bench deck (get_mission_ids_for_deck_11e) has Assassination (5 VP tactical for a CHARACTER kill), No Prisoners (2 VP per unit) and Overwhelming Force (3 VP per unit on an objective). _score_charge_target has no card term, so the over-counted ch_damage was the only thing pulling charges onto these kills. Guard s7431 r3 P1 is measured harmful (-5.00, n12). P1 holds Assassination and Overwhelming Force. The Allarus charged a 1-W Blade Champion Alpha on the centre (10 dmg vs 1 W, a 10x overkill). Blade Champion Gamma (7 W) stands 0.43 in from it, also on the centre, at 8.21 in vs 8.45 in, so both need 9+. Base target scores tie at 20+2+3+5. The fix gives 12 vs 30, so the AI most likely switches to Blade Champion Gamma. That kill is less certain (10 dmg vs 7 W), and the charge move must keep 2 in from Blade Champion Alpha (0.43 in away) and Custodian Guard Beta (0.37 in away). The designer did not check s7431 r3, although section 8 of the charge brief lists it as a guard. The finding's own alternative points the same way. At s7480, Blade Champion Alpha is a CHARACTER in base contact with P2's Blade Champion Gamma, and P2 (trailing 15-43) held Assassination. So the +5.75 is plausibly Assassination VP, not overkill. I derived this from the score terms, the saves and the cards at decision. I did not replay it.
issues.proposed_change: Skip CT-OVERKILL and CT-COMBO when destroying the target pays one of the decider's own active cards. Read them from _get_secondary_awareness(player), which the shooting scorer already uses. Exempt the target when any of these hold: its keywords match kill_keywords (Assassination gives CHARACTER; Bring It Down gives VEHICLE and MONSTER); its unit id is in marked_targets; kill_proximity is set (No Prisoners); kill_near_objectives is set and the target is within OBJECTIVE_CONTROL_RANGE_PX of an objective; kill_big_units_min is met. The simplest safe subset is to always exempt CHARACTER targets. The s7480 remnant still flips, because it is not a CHARACTER and P2 holds no card it meets. Add a real-save guard test that s7431 r3 still declares on U_BLADE_CHAMPION_A_P2, and replay s7431 r3 with the fix.

issues.situation: CT-COMBO combined with the post-roll keep rule and the non-target engagement-range rule. Combos only form when the two targets are close to each other (max_spread in _score_multi_target_combo). CT-COMBO turns [gated G + X] into [X] alone. After the roll, _select_post_roll_charge_targets keeps the declared targets that are in reach, so G is never added back. _cm_feasible then rejects every endpoint within 2 in of G, because G is now a non-target. When G is an escort or shares an objective with X (at s7431 they are 0.37-0.43 in apart), fewer models reach X or the AI sends SKIP_CHARGE ('cannot complete the charge move - charge fails'). The base declaration engaged both units.
issues.proposed_change: Keep G in combos when it is within 2 in (engagement range) of another target in the combo. Alternatively, apply CT-COMBO only when the charger cannot engage both targets: a single-model charger, or the targets on opposite sides of the charger, as at s7480.

issues.situation: The reach metric overstates how often decisions change. [CHARGE_TARGET] prints on every capped evaluation, including each repeat evaluation per declaration step and each post-roll re-scoring in _select_post_roll_charge_targets. So 45.5 lines per game says little about changed declarations, and the protocol-v2 bench-reach gate (at least 1 line per game) is met trivially.
issues.proposed_change: In _evaluate_best_charge, compute the ranking with and without the fix and log one decision-level line when the chosen declaration differs. Use that line for the reach gate and for the fires-per-fixture report.

issues.situation: Later-round cost. The fix moves charges from units the charger can kill to big units that survive the fight (Custodian Guard or Allarus at 20 W, Deffkoptas at 24 W, Stompa at 30 W). That leaves the small unit alive to hold or score next turn, and it locks the charger in a fight that lasts several rounds. ch_retaliation prices only one round of fight-back, and a one-round rollout cannot see the round after.
issues.proposed_change: Read the horizon-2 re-check of s7480 before shipping. Bench all three fixtures with full-game pairs before any decision; the single Custodes pair played so far is noise.

issues.situation: test_ai_fix_charge_target.gd uses synthetic snapshots only. It has no real-save tests: none for s7480, and none for the section-8 guards s7431 r3, s7403 r3, s7470_1 and s7466. No test covers a bench-roster case such as a full 6-W Blade Champion charged by a 5-model Custodian Guard.
issues.proposed_change: Add real-save tests with the r4 root .w40ksave harness: s7480 changes, while s7431 r3, s7470_1 and s7466 keep their logged targets. Add a bench-roster unit test that the full-health case is left unchanged once the depletion gate is in.

reviews.fires_in_bench: It fires often in the bench, and mostly not on remnants. Custodes mirror: in two bench-roster game logs with the base AI, 19 of 55 declarations (both seats) involve a target that trips the gate, mostly at full health: a lone 6-W Blade Champion or 4-W Prosecutors charged by a 5-model Custodian Guard or Allarus at 13.9 dmg. That is about 9-10 declarations per game, roughly 5 per seat. I estimate 3-6 changed declarations per game in the candidate seat, mostly multi-target declarations that CT-COMBO rewrites. This matches the designer's 45.5 lines per game, 14.5 of them combo exclusions. Asym: when the candidate plays Custodes, nearly every Custodian Guard or Allarus charge at Stormboyz, Warbikers A/B, Wartrikes or the Mek is gated at full health (estimate 4-8 changed per game). On the Ork side, mainly the Stompa against a Blade Champion, and the Stompa sits exactly on the 2x line there (12 vs 6) (estimate 0-1). Orks mirror: the Stompa against Wartrikes, Warbikers A/B and the Mek; Deffkoptas and Wazdakka against the Mek; and Gretchin or Stormboyz units already worn down (estimate 1-3). This is far above the 1.0 line per game reach gate, so the fix will show in the bench, but as a broad change. With the proposed depletion gate I estimate about 1-2 changed declarations per game. These counts are estimates from existing logs and engine damage math; I did not run the fix.
reviews.strengths:
- The principle is sound: damage past a unit's last wound is wasted.
- The change is small: two param-gated hooks. FIX_CHARGE_TARGET=0 restores the base exactly, and a test checks that.
- It reproduces the exact measured alternative at s7480 (charge the Blade Champion only, +5.75 over 24 fresh seeds).
- The designer found the second leg with a forced replay: with the cap alone the AI declared remnant + Blade Champion, which played out identically to the base (E 0.00).
- It leaves the near-exact-kill guardrails (1.02x, 1.27x) and the charge-vs-no-charge bar alone, so it does not make the AI charge less in general.
- The low-roll fallback through the post-roll re-pick keeps working.
- The report is honest that log lines are not decisions and that the full-game effect is untested.
- In the asym fixture the re-ranking is often materially better (for example, Custodian Guard into Warbikers C/D at 120 pts or Deffkoptas instead of a 45-pt Mek), so a narrowed version has real upside.
reviews.summary: The principle is sound and the finding it fixes is robust, but the rule reaches far beyond its evidence. In bench rosters the 2x gate trips at full health: full 5-model Custodian Guard and Allarus units (13.9 dmg) trip it on lone Blade Champions, Prosecutors and most small Ork units. 19 of 55 declarations in two bench-roster Custodes-mirror logs involve such a target, and CT-COMBO rewrites every multi-target declaration that lists one while the charger is at full strength. In measured play, 13 of the 14 gated charges were at lone CHARACTERs. The cap removes the only part of the charge score that tracked kill-card VP (Assassination, No Prisoners, Overwhelming Force), and nothing replaces it. It most likely flips the measured-harmful guard s7431 r3, where P1 holds Assassination and Overwhelming Force, from the 1-W Blade Champion to an adjacent 7-W one. The finding's own +5.75 is plausibly Assassination VP: P2 held the card and the better target was a CHARACTER already in combat. Revise in three steps. First, add a depletion gate (at most 50% of starting wounds left). Second, exempt targets that the decider's own kill cards pay for, at least CHARACTERs. Third, add a real-save guard test for s7431 r3, bench all three fixtures, and count changed declarations, not log lines. I did not replay anything. The s7431 r3 flip and the bench decision counts come from score terms, saves and existing logs.

issues.situation: The trigger is only 'expected melee damage >= 2x wounds left'. Nothing checks that the target is damaged, so with the bench datasheets the gate fires mostly on FULL-HEALTH units, in all three fixtures. Custodes mirror fixture (5-model Custodian Guard or Allarus, 25 spear attacks): 13.89 dmg against a full 6-W Blade Champion is 2.31x, and against the 4-W Prosecutors 2.89x. For a Custodian Guard charger the Blade Champion's target score falls from about 46.7 to 26.2, while a Custodian Guard target stays at about 18.9. So the pick flips from Blade Champion to Custodian Guard whenever p(BC)/p(CG) is between 0.40 and 0.72, and every Blade Champion and the Prosecutors drop out of Custodian Guard/Allarus multi-target declarations. Asym, Custodes seat: Custodian Guard/Allarus against the Mek is 6.9x, against all four Stormboyz units 2.31x, both 3-model Warbikers 2.31x, both Wartrikes 2.06x. The Custodes target ranking turns from Mek ~68 > Warbikers/Wartrike ~40 > Stormboyz ~36 into Deffkoptas ~36 > Gretchin ~33 > Wartrike ~25 > Warbikers ~22 > Stormboyz ~20 > Mek ~19 (my Python re-implementation of _estimate_melee_damage plus the score terms, not run in Godot). Orks mirror: Stompa against the Mek, the Wartrikes and the 3-model Warbikers, and Deffkoptas against the Mek (exactly 2.00x). None of the designer's 7 replayed positions shows a full-health target flipping a decision. At the finding's datasheets a 3-model custodes_lions Custodian Guard does 10.0 dmg to a 7-W Blade Champion (1.43x), so it never fires there. The report's root cause, risks and test cover only remnants. In practice this is a broad charge-targeting change shipped under the narrow label (the round-2 lesson).
issues.proposed_change: Gate both arms on a damaged target. Add e.g. `and ct_hp <= 0.5 * starting_wounds` (the sum of each model's 'wounds' over all models, alive or not) to the CT-OVERKILL condition in _score_charge_target and to the ct_overkill flag in _evaluate_best_charge. The s7480 remnant (2 of 6 W) still qualifies. Add a unit test where a 5-model Custodian Guard against a full 6-W Blade Champion must stay uncapped. Then re-measure bench reach on all three fixtures (asym included) as CHANGED declarations or targets per game, not log lines. If a general overkill cap is what was intended, re-label the design as broad and require the full-game bench on all three fixtures before it competes.

issues.situation: A measured-harmful position outside the cluster's guardrails flips. At s7431 r3 P1 (custodes_lions mirror), the 3-model Allarus (10.0 dmg) charged Blade Champion Alpha, which had 1 W left and stood on the centre (28%, 8.45"). Not charging measured -5.00 over 12 seeds; the separator brief links this to P1's Assassination and Overwhelming Force cards. Blade Champion Gamma (7 W) is also on the centre at 8.21" with the same 9+ roll. In the base the two score the same, (20+2)x1.3+8 = 36.6 each. With the cap BC Alpha becomes (2+2)x1.3+8 = 13.2, so the Allarus almost certainly switches to BC Gamma. Its kill chance if the charge lands drops from about 1.0 to about 0.78, and a survivor fights back. The report's harmful_moves=0 covers only the 4 listed guardrails. Of the 18 clear/harmful measured charge positions, the single-target gate touches only two, and they point opposite ways: s7431 (harmful) and s7467 r2 P1 (Allarus -> 4-W Mek, clear +2.64, n36).
issues.proposed_change: Before the design advances, replay s7431 r3 P1 (A = the base's BC Alpha charge, B = the fix's choice) and s7467 r2 P1 with the fix over 24+ seeds. If s7431 loses, leave CHARACTER targets out of CT-OVERKILL (their kill-card value is not modelled), or add a kill-value term instead of only removing the overkill credit.

issues.situation: The 2.0x gate is a step, so the target's value is not monotone in the charger's damage. A 6-model Deffkoptas unit (8.00 dmg against the 4-W Mek, 2.00x) gets ch_damage 8; a 5-model unit (6.67 dmg, 1.67x) gets 13.3. _evaluate_best_charge picks the best (unit, target) pair across all units, so a weaker unit can be preferred for the same target. Several bench pairs sit right on the step: Deffkoptas->Mek 2.00, Stompa->Blade Champion 2.00, Stompa->3-model Warbikers 2.00, Custodian Guard/Allarus->Wartrike 2.06, Blade Champion->Mek 2.08. The s7465 extra finding's Beastboss is at 1.975. A small change in the estimate decides whether the value halves.
issues.proposed_change: Make CT-OVERKILL continuous, e.g. `damage_for_value = minf(melee_damage, k * ct_hp)` with k about 1.3. This leaves the 1.02x and 1.27x guardrails untouched. The remnant gets 2.6 instead of 2, which by the designer's own numbers still keeps the single remnant charge below the Blade Champion. Keep the 2x flag only for the CT-COMBO exclusion.

issues.situation: CT-COMBO patches a symptom. The finding's real failure is in the move: _compute_charge_move places the nearest models first, and when it cannot cover every declared target it drops the uncovered one ('could not reach ... proceeding against'), which is the far, valuable target. _score_multi_target_combo's spread check (charger reach plus 4" for multi-model units) also lets such pairs through. CT-COMBO only helps when the near leg is a gross-overkill target. It also throws away real value when both targets can be engaged. The test's own combo fixture is such a case: the 2-model charger can end with one model within 2" of each target and stay in coherency. In the bench it removes every full-health Blade Champion and the Prosecutors (mirror), and the Mek, Stormboyz, Warbikers and Wartrikes (asym), from Custodes multi-target declarations.
issues.proposed_change: Limit the exclusion to remnants (as in the major issue). Or fix the cause: when the whole declared set survives the roll but the move cannot cover it, keep the highest-value subset the move can cover, in _select_post_roll_charge_targets / _compute_charge_move, instead of the nearest target.

issues.situation: [CHARGE_TARGET] prints on every capped _score_charge_target call: each repeated _evaluate_best_charge pass in a phase (one per declaration or skip), each post-roll re-score, and each combo exclusion. So the 45.5 lines per game count score changes, not decisions. That count comes from one Custodes-mirror pair, candidate seat only; asym, where the trigger is broadest, was not measured. Protocol v2's 'at least 1 line per game' gate becomes trivially passed and tells nothing. The designer prompt asked for a log line when the fix changes a decision.
issues.proposed_change: Keep the existing lines. Add one '[CHARGE_TARGET] changed' line per decision when the fix's pick differs from the uncapped pick (compute both in _evaluate_best_charge), and report that count per fixture.

issues.situation: Test coverage stops at a 2-W remnant. The test is otherwise sound: it drives _decide_charge, pins the fix on and erases the override, runs at Competitive (zero noise), and fails 3 of 8 checks on base for the right reason. The combo case fails if CT-COMBO is removed: on CT-OVERKILL alone the combo still wins, EV ~24.9 vs 21.3. Missing: a full-health small-target case, which is the dominant bench trigger and would have exposed the major issue, and any post-roll case, although _select_post_roll_charge_targets also uses the capped score. The combo test also asserts dropping the remnant from a two-target charge the unit could actually make, which is the opposite of the finding's failure mode.
issues.proposed_change: Add three cases. (a) A 5-model Custodian Guard against a full 6-W Blade Champion: the cap must not fire once the major issue is fixed. (b) Two post-roll cases: a low roll leaves only the remnant selectable (it must still be picked), and both the remnant and a fresh unit are selectable. (c) A combo fixture where the charge move cannot engage both targets.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Evaluation level: it fires in every game of all three fixtures, because the 2x gate trips on FULL-HEALTH targets with the bench datasheets. Custodes mirror: every 5-model Custodian Guard/Allarus evaluation of a 6-W Blade Champion (2.31x) or the Prosecutors (2.89x), plus any remnant at or below ~6.9 W. Asym, Custodes seat: Custodian Guard/Allarus against the Mek (6.9x), all four Stormboyz (2.31x), both 3-model Warbikers (2.31x) and both Wartrikes (2.06x); Blade Champion against the Mek (2.08x). Asym, Orks seat: Stompa against a Blade Champion (2.00x). Orks mirror: Stompa against the Mek, Wartrikes and 3-model Warbikers; Deffkoptas against the Mek (2.00x); Wazdakka against the Mek; plus remnants (Gretchin, Stormboyz) from round 2 on. The designer's 41-50 lines per game (Custodes mirror, 1 pair, candidate seat) fits this; the lines repeat for each evaluation pass and post-roll re-score. Changed declarations or targets: my estimate from the score shifts, not run. Custodes mirror about 1-3 per game: for a Custodian Guard the Blade Champion's score falls from ~46.7 to ~26.2 against a Custodian Guard target at ~18.9, so the pick flips when p(BC)/p(CG) is 0.40-0.72, and Blade Champions/Prosecutors leave every Custodian Guard/Allarus combo. Asym about 2-5 per game when the candidate plays Custodes (the target ranking reorders: Mek ~68 to ~19, Stormboyz ~36 to ~20, Warbikers ~40 to ~22, while Deffkoptas ~36 and Gretchin ~33 are unchanged), about 0-1 when it plays Orks. Orks mirror about 0.5-2 per game, mostly the Stompa and Deffkoptas switching from Mek/Wartrikes/small units to Deffkoptas or the enemy Stompa. It clears the bench-reach gate easily, but it is a broad charge-targeting change (full_game_safety), not a narrow one.
reviews.strengths: The patch is small and readable, and fully gated: FIX_CHARGE_TARGET=0 restores base decisions exactly. Both arms check the param, the post-roll path inherits the gate through _score_charge_target, and combo_targets aliases scored_targets at 0. The only side effects are the inert ct_overkill=false key and the param-read entries in decision records. The flag and the score use the same inputs (_estimate_melee_damage, _calculate_kill_threshold), so they cannot disagree. There is no null-access risk, the extra cost per candidate is negligible, comments and [CHARGE_TARGET] logs are clear, and no debug log was removed. The root-cause trace at s7480 r3 P2 is correct. I verified the 7.5 dmg against a 2-W remnant (18 x 5/6 x 1/2 x 1/2 x 2), the nearest-first move coverage that turned 'remnant + Blade Champion' into a remnant-only charge, and the 11e post-roll fallback (ChargePhase ~906-925 plus _select_post_roll_charge_targets) that backs CT-COMBO's claim that a low roll still re-picks the remnant. The fix lands exactly on the measured alternative (Blade Champion only, +5.75 n24). The 4 listed guardrails sit at 1.01/1.27/0.30/0.66x, so they cannot fire. The test drives the real _decide_charge path, pins the fix on and erases the override, runs at Competitive (deterministic), isolates CT-COMBO from CT-OVERKILL, and fails on base for the right reason (the capped term, the single-target pick and the combo pick: 5 pass, 3 fail). The risk section openly says log lines are not decisions and combo value can be lost.
reviews.summary: Verdict: revise. The code is clean and exactly gated, the test drives the real decision path, and the design fixes the s7480 finding exactly (Blade Champion only, +5.75). The problem is scope. The trigger is 'expected damage >= 2x wounds left' with no damaged-target condition, so with the bench datasheets it mostly fires on full-health units, not remnants. In the Custodes mirror every 5-model Custodian Guard/Allarus evaluation of a 6-W Blade Champion is capped (target score ~46.7 to ~26.2) and those Blade Champions drop out of multi-target declarations. In asym the Custodes target ranking reorders: Mek ~68 to ~19, Stormboyz/Warbikers/Wartrikes down 40-50%, Deffkoptas and Gretchin unchanged and now on top. The design was evaluated on one pair in one fixture. It also very likely swaps the target at the measured-harmful s7431 r3 P1, from the 1-W Blade Champion on the centre (charging it was measured right, E -5.00) to the full Blade Champion Gamma; nobody checked that. Two smaller problems: the step at exactly 2.0x is non-monotone in the charger's damage, and several bench pairs sit on it; and CT-COMBO patches a charge-move coverage defect only for overkill targets. To revise: gate both arms on damaged targets, use a continuous cap, replay s7431 and s7467, add full-health and post-roll tests, and count changed declarations (not log lines) on all three fixtures. Not run: I made no Godot runs (read-only lens). The bench ratios and scores come from my Python re-implementation of the AI's estimates on the decoded fixture saves (40k/tests/saves/*_postdeploy.w40ksave), and the s7431 analysis comes from the decoded case save (40k/tests/rollout_cases/r2c00/s7431_r3_p1_charge_1.w40ksave). Reviewed files: /home/user/warhammer-40k-godot/.ai_lab_work/wt_panel_ct/tools/ai_lab/r5_designs/charge_target/narrow.patch and narrow.json.

issues.situation: CT-CAP (_score_charge_target) caps ch_damage at _calculate_kill_threshold(target). That count covers only the target's own models and has no kill-certainty term. So a near-certain kill of a nearly dead target loses most of its value: the kill bonuses are a flat +5/+3, and the uncapped credit was the only part that grew with kill margin. Meanwhile a leader inside an Attached unit still looks like a killable 7-W model. Measured conflict: s7431 r3 P1 is class harmful (E -5.00). Charging the lone 1-W Blade Champion Alpha on the centre was right; in the game lens the kill paid Assassination + Overwhelming Force + destroyed-on-objective, about +11 VP. The separator brief section 8 requires this guard to keep its logged target. I applied the patch math to the logged candidates (c5_A_s7431_r3_p1_1/A_5001.record.json): Blade Champion Alpha goes 13.72 -> 5.0 and Blade Champion Gamma 13.72 -> 10.8, so the Allarus (10 expected damage) switch to Gamma. In the save, Gamma leads a live 3-model Custodian Guard Sodality Beta (15 W): a 22-W Attached unit the Allarus cannot kill, priced as a killable 7-W model with no retaliation cost. The design report did not check this position. Bench form (the bench has no Attached units): a Custodes charger with 10-14 expected damage chooses between a lone Blade Champion or a remnant shot down to 1-4 W and a healthier target. In the V10 reach game cus_95002 R3, the cap moves Custodian Guard Beta off a 4-W lone Blade Champion (68.3 -> 34.4) onto a full 20-W Custodian Guard unit (47.4). 11 of 19 Custodes-mirror declarations had a capped candidate. The one-round rollout also misses a later cost: a target that survives keeps the charger locked in combat next turn.
issues.proposed_change: Exempt CHARACTER targets from CT-CAP and keep the base credit for them. A fuller version replaces the hard cap with E[min(D, HP)] plus a P(kill)-weighted kill value, and sums HP over the whole Attached unit (19.02) before the cap and the can_wipe/can_halve/retaliation tests. Re-scored with the exemption: s7431 keeps Blade Champion Alpha (same 13.72/13.72 tie as the base). The finding f1 then picks its measured +5.75 alternative, Blade Champion Alpha single (32.9 + 3.1 fallback = 36.0), over Allarus #2 (9.8 + 25.0 = 34.8) and the remnant combo (about 25). The current fix declares [Allarus #2] there instead. Also add s7431 r3 and s7403 r3 replays (logged targets kept) as guard tests. Put CT-CAP and CT-FALLBACK on separate sub-params so the bench can attribute effects.

issues.situation: CT-FALLBACK lets a single far declaration win on fallback value. At f1, Allarus #2 at 9+ wins with +20.36 of fallback. ChargePhase._check_command_reroll_or_resolve offers the re-roll using the distance to the nearest DECLARED target, before the 11e selectable re-filter. evaluate_command_reroll_charge then re-rolls any miss with need <= 9 when CP >= 3, gap <= 2 or roll <= 4; the free ability re-roll always re-rolls a miss. So a roll that already reaches the fallback is spent on a 1-CP re-roll, which can land below every target. The new EV term assumes the first roll stands. This is rare in the bench: Custodes buy FURY OF THE EMPEROR at declaration, 15.01 then blocks a second stratagem on that unit, and bench Orks almost never declare. It does matter for other armies.
issues.proposed_change: At edition >= 11, make the charge re-roll decision fallback-aware. Either compute 'needed' from the nearest enemy the post-roll step would charge (the selectable / _charge_post_roll_fallback_ev pool), or re-roll only when EV(re-roll) under the same 2D6 model beats EV(keep) plus a CP cost.

issues.situation: _charge_coordination records the declared target. V10 has FIX_CHARGE_EV = 0, so later chargers get KILL GANG-UP (+5/+7) and pile-on bonuses toward a far declared target the first unit usually did not reach, because it re-picked the fallback on most rolls. Meanwhile the unit it actually engaged has no coordination entry. The fix makes far singles with fallbacks more common, so this mis-coordination happens more often (Ork gang-up bonuses are the largest).
issues.proposed_change: When _select_post_roll_charge_targets re-picks, move the unit's _charge_coordination entry from the dropped declared target to the re-picked one. Alternatively, enable CH-ARRIVED from FIX_CHARGE_EV in this arm.

issues.situation: _charge_post_roll_fallback_ev values each fallback at score/prob. That value keeps the CHARGE_SHORT_6IN/3IN reliability multipliers (x1.2, x1.56), although the fallback is only charged on specific low rolls. With a very near fallback this inflates far declarations; the designer saw +62 on a 10+ target. Through unit_best it also reorders which unit charges first in _build_charge_order.
issues.proposed_change: Divide the ch_short_charge multiplier out of the fallback value; keep the objective, leave and overwatch multipliers. Rank units for charge order on the score without the fallback term if the bench shows order churn.

issues.situation: bench_fires_per_game = 104 counts [CHARGE_TARGET] lines, not changed decisions. The CT-CAP line prints on every capped evaluation, which repeats at every declaration step and in post-roll re-picks. The fallback line prints for every single target that has a nearer alternative, also in phases that end with no charge. So the V2-1 log-tag gate will pass in all 3 fixtures whether or not any decision changes. The broad rescoring also rests on one clear finding. At f1 the BC alternative's gain came with a material loss (mat -123 in the 12-seed check). Per the designer's A/B, it came largely from P2's Punishment condemned_left +5 for units that were not the charge target (the save's condemned list is P1's Custodian Guard B, Blade Champion Gamma and Custodian Guard C). The fix's own choice at f1 measured +4.58 [-1.29, 10.46] over 12 seeds.
issues.proposed_change: Log a [CHARGE_TARGET] line only when the chosen declaration or re-pick differs from the FIX=0 choice (compute both), and report changed declarations per fixture. Bench CT-CAP and CT-FALLBACK as separate sub-params.

reviews.fires_in_bench: Log lines: about 104 per game (designer's figure, Custodes mirror only). Both tags print on evaluations whose result does not change, so the V2-1 tag gate passes trivially in all three fixtures. Changed decisions are far fewer. I re-scored the V10 reach games offline (rounds 1-3 only; the runs stop at round 4) with the patch's CT-CAP and CT-FALLBACK math. Inputs: /root/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/40k/test_results/fx10_reach/{cus_95002,asy_99002,ork_94002}.record.json; script: /tmp/review_ct/rescore.py. This is an approximation, not a Godot run: only the chosen unit's candidates are recorded, and combo hits-back values are unknown. Results: Custodes mirror, 2 definite changed declarations out of 19, plus about 5 combo-vs-single near-ties. Both definite changes moved Custodian Guard units off a 4-W lone Blade Champion that another unit had already declared at, onto a 20-W Custodian Guard unit. Asym: 0 out of 12, plus 4 near-ties where the first target stays the same. Ork mirror: 0 out of 1, because the Orks almost never declare. At least one capped candidate appeared in 11/19 and 6/12 Custodes declarations. Charge/no-charge is essentially unchanged: 0 flips in 67 no-charge records in cus/asy, and one upper-bound flip in the Ork mirror (round 2, Stormboyz at 8%) that CT-CAP probably cancels. Extrapolated to 5 rounds: about 2-4 changed declarations per Custodes-mirror game, 0-2 per asym game and about 0 per Ork-mirror game, so roughly 1-2 per game pooled. Unit-order and post-roll re-pick changes come on top and are not visible in the records. Almost all the reach comes from CT-CAP; CT-FALLBACK alone rarely flips a bench declaration.
reviews.strengths: CT-FALLBACK follows the engine: under 11e 11.04 targets are picked after the roll, and the new term mirrors _select_post_roll_charge_targets. It picks the fallback by raw target_score and values it as score/prob, the same value-if-reached the combos use. So single-target and multi-target declarations are finally compared like for like. There is no recursion or double count: the fallback uses the stored single scores, and a combo gets fallback only for rolls below its nearest member. It is param-gated (0 = base), the test fails on the base and passes on the fix, and the related tests pass. Charge/no-charge does not change, so it does not 'charge less', as the hint required. The cluster guardrails keep their choices (s7465_r2_p2, s7470_r2_p2, s7466, s7480_r3_p1), and by my re-score so do s7403 r3 and both twins s7469/s7470_1. In the bench, CT-CAP partly stands in for the gated-off CH-NEEDED: it moves follow-up chargers off a target that another unit has already over-killed. The designer's report is candid about lines not being decisions, the broad effect, and its partial match at f1.
reviews.summary: Revise. The idea behind CT-FALLBACK (value a declaration as its expected value over 2D6, including the post-roll re-pick) is sound and rarely flips a bench decision on its own. CT-CAP is the part that acts broadly. It rescales every overkill charge evaluation and the post-roll re-pick, using the target's own models' wounds with no kill-certainty term. That flips a measured-right target at s7431 r3 (harmful class, a required guard): the Allarus leave a near-certain kill of a lone 1-W Blade Champion for a Blade Champion who leads a 15-W bodyguard. The design report did not catch this. In the bench (no Attached units) the cap changes about 10% of Custodes declarations, usually moving chargers off wounded lone characters. Some of those moves may help, where other units had already over-committed to the target, but they are unmeasured. The design's support is one finding whose gain is partly mission-driven, and the fix does not even choose that finding's measured alternative. Concrete change: exempt CHARACTER targets from the cap, or use E[min(D,HP)] plus a P(kill) value and Attached-unit HP. With the exemption, s7431 keeps its target and f1 picks the measured Blade Champion alternative (≈36.0 against ≈34.8). Add s7431 r3/s7403 r3 guard replays and split CT-CAP and CT-FALLBACK into sub-params. Minor: the re-roll windows judge the roll against declared targets, the coordination record keeps the declared far target, short-charge multipliers are counted in the fallback value, and the reach counts lines rather than decisions. I did not run Godot; all numbers come from offline re-scoring of the recorded decisions and saves.

issues.situation: Re-roll logic undoes the fallback value. CT-FALLBACK now often declares a far target and counts on the post-roll re-pick when the roll falls short. At s7480 r3 P2 the fix declares [Allarus #2] alone (9+); 20.36 of its 30.19 score comes from charging Blade Champion on 5-8 and the remnant on 3-4. The re-roll path does not know about this fallback. ChargePhase._check_command_reroll_or_resolve (ChargePhase.gd ~730-775) sets roll_context.min_distance from charge_data.targets, which still holds the declared targets because the 11e filter runs later in _resolve_charge_roll. AIPlayer._on_command_reroll_opportunity then calls evaluate_command_reroll_charge(total, need=9). That re-rolls on 7-8 (gap <= 2), on 2-4 (roll <= 4), and on 5-6 when CP >= 3. So the AI pays 1 CP, and uses up its once-per-phase COMMAND RE-ROLL, on exactly the rolls the fix credits as successes. On a 7 it gives up a certain Blade Champion charge for a fresh 2D6. P2 has 2 CP at the finding, so about 17/36 of rolls trigger it. Base's [remnant, A#2] declaration has need 3, so base re-rolls only on a 2. The free path in _on_ability_reroll_opportunity has the same problem (total < declared need). In the bench, FURY OF THE EMPEROR needs an ingress move, so it never blocks the re-roll. Raised fallback scores also push these units earlier in the charge order, so they use the phase's re-roll first.
issues.proposed_change: Make the charge re-roll check aware of the fallback under the same parameter (FIX_CHARGE_TARGET > 0 and edition >= 11). Add the provisional charge_data.selectable_targets (already computed in _process_charge_roll before the re-roll window) to roll_context. In both AIPlayer re-roll handlers, treat the roll as made when a selectable enemy is in reach. Better: compare the value-if-reached of the best raw-score target in reach with the declaration's fresh-roll EV minus a CP cost, through a new AIDecisionMaker helper that takes unit_id. Add a test: declared [far], roll inside the fallback band, expect DECLINE_COMMAND_REROLL at param 1 and the old re-roll at param 0.

issues.situation: The decision test does not exercise CT-FALLBACK; CT-CAP alone passes it. _test_finding_charges_the_valuable_target expects ['champ']. Computed by hand from the base code (not run), with CT-CAP on and the fallback off: remnant = (2*2 + 3 + 3 + 5) x 1.0 x 1.2 x 1.3 = 23.4; champ = (7*2 + 2 + 3 + 5) x 0.833 x 1.2 = 24.0; combo [remnant, far] = 23.4 (both extra shares are 0). Both damage values are capped, so these numbers do not depend on the exact damage estimate. Champ wins without any fallback. So if ct_fallback_on were forced false, or the fallback were wired in wrong (wrong declared ids, wrong roll band), every decision-level test would still pass. The single-unit fallback code, the charge_eval and unit_best updates, and the combo pool are checked only through the helper _charge_post_roll_fallback_ev. The expected 'champ' is also not what the fix does at the real finding, which is an A#2 single driven by the fallback. The assert message credits 'remnant as the post-roll fallback', which is misleading.
issues.proposed_change: Add a decision test through _decide_charge where CT-CAP does nothing (no expected damage above remaining wounds) and only the fallback changes the declaration. Example: a single-model charger, a high-value target at 9+, a mid target at 5+ on the opposite side (combo not feasible), and a near weak target. Assert the declared ids and that the chosen candidate's record has a ch_post_roll_fallback term. Assert the base declaration and no fallback term at FIX_CHARGE_TARGET=0. Optionally drive APPLY_CHARGE_MOVE with selectable=[mid] on a 6 to pin the re-pick the model assumes. Fix the existing assert message so it says CT-CAP is what decides that case.

issues.situation: _charge_coordination records the wrong target. It records the declared target (FIX_CHARGE_EV is off in V10), not the target actually charged after a re-pick. Under the fix, far singles that rely on the fallback (for example 'Beastboss 8% + 0.15 fallback' at s7465, or 28% A#2) usually end up engaging a different unit. Later chargers then get gang-up or pile-on bonuses (Orks +7 / +3 per charger) toward a unit the first charger mostly missed. They also lose the T19-5 seed bonus on it, and the unit really engaged gets no coordination entry. Base had the same mismatch for combos; the fix makes it much more frequent.
issues.proposed_change: Under the parameter, in _decide_charge step 2, after _select_post_roll_charge_targets re-targets, move this charger's _charge_coordination entry from the dropped declared ids to the targets actually charged. Alternatively, require a small margin before a fallback-heavy far single beats the best near single, since the realized gain is often tiny (at s7465 it is a tie-break).

issues.situation: Value-if-reached (score / prob) still includes ch_short_charge, which is x1.2 or x1.56 for 'reliable' charges. In the fallback, probability is already summed roll by roll, so near fallback targets count reliability twice. At f1 that inflates both pieces of the +20.36 (Blade Champion x1.2, remnant x1.56). This tips declarations toward 'far target, near fallback'; the critic flagged ch_short_charge as part of the original error. The base combos use the same convention, so the comparison is still like for like.
issues.proposed_change: Under the parameter, strip the ch_short_charge factor from value-if-reached in _charge_post_roll_fallback_ev and in _score_multi_target_combo. Or keep it and record the choice in the design notes.

issues.situation: Explanation and logging. A far single is described as 'declares charge against A#2 (28% chance ...)', and the unit-order tag says '28% to make it', although the declaration charges some enemy about 97% of the time. A combo's fallback amount is added to its EV but never logged under [CHARGE_TARGET]. ch_post_roll_fallback has no AIReasoningGlossary entry, and the ch_damage help text ('expected damage x weight') is now wrong when the cap applies.
issues.proposed_change: Add the fallback plan to best_description (for example '; Blade Champion on 5-8, remnant on 3-4'). Print the combo fallback with the tag. Add a glossary entry and update the ch_damage help text.

issues.situation: Coupling and scope. The fallback model hard-codes the current _select_post_roll_charge_targets behaviour (always re-pick the best raw score, never decline under 11.02). Any change there would make the fallback credit wrong, for example declining weak re-picks (another round-5 angle). The fallback also uses plain 2D6 and ignores charge-roll modifiers (+1/+2); this is inherited from base. Outside the bench, CT-CAP caps credit at the bodyguard unit's own wounds, so it would undervalue damage that carries over to an attached leader. The bench has no attached units.
issues.proposed_change: Put the re-pick rule behind one shared helper used by both _select_post_roll_charge_targets and _charge_post_roll_fallback_ev, or add a cross-reference comment. Note the attached-unit caveat before any non-bench rollout.

issues.situation: Test hygiene. AIDecisionMaker._current_difficulty is set to COMPETITIVE and never restored. The param-0 test only checks ch_damage and ids != ['champ']; it does not check that the base declaration is exact or that the fallback term is absent. There is no test of the edition < 11 gate and none of CT-CAP's effect on the post-roll re-pick ranking.
issues.proposed_change: Restore the difficulty setting. Assert the exact base ids and the absence of ch_post_roll_fallback at param 0. Add one edition-10 assert (no fallback term) and one post-roll re-pick assert with CT-CAP on.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
These are my estimates from the trigger conditions; I did not run Godot. It fires in all 3 fixtures, because nothing depends on reserves or attached units. Log tag: about 50-150 [CHARGE_TARGET] lines per game. CT-CAP prints on every over-kill pair at every declaration step and at every post-roll re-score. The fallback prints for every non-nearest single with a nearer scored target. So the protocol-v2 reach gate (>= 1 line per game) passes trivially; the designer's 55/153 lines (Custodes mirror only) fit this. Those lines count re-scores, not changed decisions, and the Ork fixtures were not run.

Changed decisions:
- CT-FALLBACK changes the declared target when a unit has 2+ targets at different roll needs, the farther one has the higher value-if-reached, and a combo is not feasible or ties. This is common for single-model chargers: Blade Champions and split Allarus Lions in Custodes; Wartrikes, Wazdakka, Deffkoptas and Stompa in Kult of Speed.
- CT-CAP re-ranks targets when expected damage exceeds wounds left: Prosecutors, remnants, 6-7W characters, Mek, Gretchin.
- Per game in the fix seat: about 1-3 changed declarations in the Custodes mirror and 2-5 in each Ork fixture. About half of these change the unit actually engaged; the rest differ only on high rolls or in which declared target is named.
- Side effect: extra COMMAND RE-ROLLs (1 CP each) after far-single declarations with need <= 9, plausibly 0.5-1.5 per game in the fix seat.

This is a broad change that rescores most charge evaluations, so it belongs in the full_game_safety class.
reviews.strengths:
- **Root cause holds in the code.** Over-kill damage was counted in ch_damage and again in the kill bonuses (ch_can_halve +3, ch_can_wipe +5). Singles were scored as P x V while combos (T7-50) were already scored as an EV over 2D6, so the two were not comparable.
- **The fallback matches the engine.** When the roll drops every declared target, ChargePhase._resolve_charge_roll judges success from the selectable list (target_ids empty), and the AI re-picks the best raw _score_charge_target in reach. The helper credits exactly those rolls (below the nearest declared need) and does not overlap the combo EV.
- **Param 0 restores base exactly.** The fallback is gated by ct_fallback_on, which also requires edition >= 11. Combos get an empty pool, so they add exactly +0.0. CT-CAP is behind get_param. The only change at param 0 is an extra ow_dmg key in scored_targets that nothing reads.
- **No access or cost risks.** Every key the new code reads is present. Tie-breaks keep the base order. Decision-record terms still sum to the score. The cost is negligible (O(11·n·k) per call, plus one kill-threshold sum per target score). No debug logs were removed.
- **The report is honest and its numbers check out.** A#2 30.19 = 9.83 + 5/36 x 22.19 + 20/36 x 31.10. It calls f1 a partial match, f2 not matched, and states that the bench lines are score changes, not decisions.
- **It reaches the bench.** CT-CAP is a small, principled change, and the kill bonuses still reward finishing a unit.
- **The test** sets the override on and erases it, sets and restores the edition, and fails on base for the right reasons (CT-CAP and the base declaration).
reviews.summary:
I recommend revise: two major issues, each with a concrete fix. The idea is sound and the gating is clean, so dropping it is not warranted.

The design makes two changes behind FIX_CHARGE_TARGET:
- **CT-CAP** caps the ch_damage credit at the target's remaining wounds.
- **CT-FALLBACK** adds the post-roll re-pick EV, for rolls that miss every declared target, to single and combo declarations.

Both match the code and the 11e engine. Param 0 is exactly base, and the change is cheap and safe to apply.

**Major issue 1: the re-roll logic works against the fallback.** The fix now often declares a far target and relies on the fallback (for example A#2 at 9+ at the main finding). The charge re-roll check (ChargePhase roll_context.min_distance -> AIPlayer -> evaluate_command_reroll_charge, plus the free ability re-roll) still measures need from the declared targets. So the AI spends 1 CP, and its once-per-phase COMMAND RE-ROLL, on exactly the rolls the fallback credits, including giving up a certain Blade Champion charge on a 7. Base's combo did not do this.

**Major issue 2: the decision test does not test CT-FALLBACK.** By my hand calculation from the code (not run), CT-CAP alone already picks champ: 24.0 against remnant 23.4 and combo 23.4. So the fallback is pinned only through the helper, and the test's expected outcome is not what the fix does at the real finding.

**Minor issues:**
- Coordination still records the declared far target, not the target actually charged.
- The short-charge reliability multiplier is counted again in fallback values.
- The description and glossary do not mention the fallback.
- The fallback model is tied to the current re-pick rule.
- Test hygiene gaps (difficulty not restored, weak param-0 checks).

**Bench reach:** it fires in all 3 fixtures. I estimate about 1-5 changed declarations per game (about half change the unit actually engaged) and about 50-150 log lines per game, so it is a broad full_game_safety change. Its only direct evidence is the fix's own choice at f1: +4.58 over 12 seeds, with a CI that crosses 0.

issues.situation: CH-OVERKILL is a broad rescoring, and its evidence points both ways. It applies to every charger with 2 or more targets at 3% or better: 17 of the 32 charge declarations in the three recorded V10 bench games (/root/.local/share/godot/app_userdata/40k/test_results/fx10_reach/{cus_95002,asy_99002,ork_94002}.record.json, rounds 1-3). Among targets the charger would destroy, it ranks by wounds left. The 11e kill cards pay per unit destroyed, not per wound: No Prisoners 2 VP per unit, Overwhelming Force 3 VP per unit near an objective, Assassination 5 VP. Example: a Custodian Guard (13.9 expected damage) can destroy a Blade Champion or a Lion-split 1-model Allarus (4 W, scored 8+3+5 after the cap) and can also reach a full Custodian Guard (27.8+3-13.9). After the cap these score about the same. Recorded example: in cus_95002 R3 P1, Custodian Guard Beta switches from the 4-W Blade Champion Gamma (68.3 drops to 34.4) to the full Custodian Guard Gamma (47.4). Conflict with a measured position: s7431 r3 P1 is class harmful (-5.00). There the Allarus charge at the lone 1-W Blade Champion Alpha on the centre was the right call, and P1 holds Assassination. Rescoring its decision record exactly (rollout/c5_A_s7431_r3_p1_1/A_5001.record.json) gives Blade Champion Alpha 13.72 -> 4.95 and Blade Champion Gamma 13.72 -> 10.80. So the fix charges Blade Champion Gamma, the 7-W leader of the Attached Custodian Guard Sodality Beta (22 W). No character kill follows (attacks resolve to the bodyguard), and the whole unit fights back. The only supporting position, s7480, is the same kind of choice (two single-model targets the charger would destroy: the 2-W Allarus remnant vs the 7-W Blade Champion Alpha), decided the other way. Its gain also has a different cause. In the save, Blade Champion Alpha is in base contact with P2's own Blade Champion C (edge about 0.01"), so killing it frees that unit. The base FOCUS-CHARGE bonus exists for exactly this case, but it never fires in the Charge phase: flags.is_engaged is set only inside FightPhase, and no unit in the s7480 save carries it. Meanwhile the bench's real overkill is untouched. That overkill is many units piling onto one target: in cus_95002 R2 P2, 7 declarations all target the 8-HP Custodian Guard Alpha. Chargers with only one target keep their uncapped score, and the gang-up bonus still adds +5.
issues.proposed_change: Split the parameter. FIX_CHARGE_TARGET keeps only CH-EXTRA. Move CH-OVERKILL behind its own parameter (for example FIX_CHARGE_OVERKILL, default 0) and bench it only as a separate switch arm. If s7480 needs a fix, target its actual cause: make FOCUS-CHARGE detect engagement from geometry (a friendly unit with _get_closest_model_distance_inches to the target <= engagement range) instead of reading flags.is_engaged. Then replay s7480 and s7431 r3 for that change.

issues.situation: CH-EXTRA splits Attached units in real games, and the bench cannot see this. Outside the bench, leaders are attached as standard (2-3 per side in every measured-position save). The engine and the AI list the leader and its bodyguard as two separate charge targets. The base AI's 2-target declaration [bodyguard + leader] is how it charges a whole Attached unit: 16 of the 30 measured multi-target declarations are such pairs (s7431_r2_p2, s7434_r3_p1, s7437_r3_p2_2_15, s7439, s7442, s7451, s7458, s7461, s7464, s7468 x2, s7472, s7475, s7477, s7488, s7490). Both members hit back for more than the 0.2 lock-down share, so CH-EXTRA drops the combo and declares one member alone. The design's own s7461 check shows this: it picks 'Beastboss alone', the leader of the Beast Snagga Boyz. The other member then counts as a non-target in ChargePhase._validate_engagement_range_constraints and in the AI's _compute_charge_move (non_target_models). No charging model may end within 2" of it, even though it stands in coherency with the target. In the 88 V10 game-lens logs (.ai_lab_work/charge_r5/game_lens/game_logs), single declarations at Blade Champions (mostly attached leaders) failed the charge move after a successful roll 11 times in 60. For multi-target declarations it was 2 in 65, and for other single targets 7 in 205. When such a charge does land, the fight resolves to the bodyguard anyway. All 3 bench fixtures have leader_attachments {}, so the shipping bench cannot catch this regression.
issues.proposed_change: Fold Attached units before the CH-EXTRA test. In _score_multi_target_combo, never set dead_extra for a member that belongs to the same Attached unit as another combo member (RulesEngine.attached_unit_component_ids or _attached_unit_target_id). In any single declaration left after a drop or collapse, include all components of the top target's Attached unit. Add a unit test with an attached Blade Champion + Custodian Guard pair: the declaration must still carry both ids.

issues.situation: CH-EXTRA drops a combo instead of collapsing it to one target. The single-target scores that remain lack the 11.04 fallback that the post-roll re-pick already provides: declare the far, better target, and a short roll re-picks the near one. So the fix often declares the near, lower-value target alone and never takes the better one on a high roll. Bench examples: in cus_95002 R3 P2, Custodian Guard Delta [CG Gamma 7+ + Blade Champion Beta 10+] becomes CG Gamma alone (9.2), although declaring Blade Champion Beta with the re-pick is worth about 11.3 on the fix's own capped values. In asy_99002 R2 P2, Wazdakka [CG Beta 5+ + 1-W Allarus #2 11+] becomes CG Beta alone. Related risk (frequency not verified in the bench): when the dropped extra stands next to the top target, the single declaration may have no legal endpoint outside the extra's engagement range. Example: cus_95002 R3 P1, Blade Champion Gamma at 2.3" and Custodian Guard Gamma at 3.3".
issues.proposed_change: When dead_extra is set, rewrite the combo's action to declare only the top-value target (plus its Attached components) instead of using `continue`, and keep the combo's EV (dead extras add 0). Also keep a dead extra in the declaration when any of its models is within engagement range plus one base of the top target.

issues.situation: The cap's scope is inconsistent. ct_cap counts every target at 3% or better as a real choice, including an 11+ long shot or a target scored 0. Chargers with one target stay uncapped in the same best-score comparison, so the cap also changes which unit declares first. The post-roll re-pick (_select_post_roll_charge_targets) still uses uncapped scores.
issues.proposed_change: If CH-OVERKILL is kept, count only targets with a positive score and p >= 0.3, and pass cap_overkill to the re-pick too.

issues.situation: The reach and evidence figures overstate the case. The 245 lines per game are log lines, printed once per dropped combo per evaluation, not changed decisions. The single bench pair (E -2.5, margins -53/-48) carries no information. No full game has been measured with the fix; s7480 rests on one-round rollouts.
issues.proposed_change: Log the base choice vs the fix choice once per declaration and report changed declarations per game per fixture. Bench CH-EXTRA (with the fold and collapse) on its own first.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
Both parts fire in every Custodes-mirror and asym game. Both are rare in the Orks mirror.

CH-EXTRA: V10 makes about 8 / 9 / 1.5 multi-target declarations per game (cus / asy / ork). Source: reach_v10 counted 16 / 18 / 3 GameEventLog lines containing 'targets picked after the roll', and each declaration logs 2 such lines. The fx10_reach records agree: 5 such declarations in rounds 1-3 of cus_95002 and 4 in asy_99002. Rescoring the 9 recorded bench combos, 7 lose a dead extra. The other 2 are kept because their extras hit back weakly (Prosecutors; Gretchin or Deffkoptas). That gives about 6 / 7 / 1 changed declarations per game.

CH-OVERKILL: 17 of the 32 recorded bench declarations are scored under the cap. Only 1 directly switched target in rounds 1-3 (cus R3 P1 Custodian Guard Beta). More are likely in rounds 4-5 as units are worn down, and the cap also changes the order in which units charge.

Total: about 7-10 changed declarations per game in the Custodes mirror and asym, and about 1-2 in the Orks mirror. That is far above the 1.0-per-game reach gate. The designer's 245 lines per game count log lines per evaluation, not decisions. The Attached-unit harm (issue 2) fires 0 times in the bench, because no fixture has Attached units.
reviews.strengths:
CH-EXTRA fixes a real artefact. Several base multi-target declarations are exact floating-point ties: the combo's EV equals the top target's single score to about 1e-14. Examples: cus_95002 R2 P2 Blade Champion Beta [CG Alpha + CG Zeta], cus_95002 R3 P1 CG Gamma [Blade Champion Gamma + CG Gamma], s7457 R3 P1, and s7467 R2 P2. In these, the combo wins only by rounding, yet on high rolls the charger then also engages a full-strength enemy unit (92% of rolls at cus R3 P1). By the AI's own model that extra adds nothing and hits back hard.

The design is fully gated (0 restores base behaviour exactly) and has a test that fails on base. Related tests pass. It never turns a charge into no charge for a charger with one target, and it does not touch movement, so it avoids round 2's holding-back failure. It fires well above the reach gate. The decision checks are honest: they disclose that s7465 still charges.
reviews.summary:
This design bundles a sound, narrow fix (CH-EXTRA: drop multi-target declarations whose extra target adds nothing) with a broad, weakly supported rescoring (CH-OVERKILL). As written, CH-EXTRA also breaks charges against Attached units.

CH-OVERKILL changes how about half of all bench charges are scored. It ranks targets the charger would destroy by wounds left, while the 11e kill cards pay per unit destroyed. It flips the measured-harmful position s7431 r3 onto an Attached leader. Its one supporting position, s7480, makes the same kind of choice the other way, and that gain more likely came from killing a target already in base contact with P2's own Blade Champion. That is the case the base FOCUS-CHARGE bonus is for, and it never fires because flags.is_engaged is set only in FightPhase. It also leaves the bench's real overkill untouched: many units piling onto one target.

CH-EXTRA declares only one member of an Attached unit. 16 of the 30 measured multi-target declarations are such leader + bodyguard pairs, including the design's own s7461 choice ('Beastboss alone'). In the base logs, single declarations at attached Blade Champions fail the charge move about 18% of the time, against about 3% for multi-target declarations. The bench cannot see this because no fixture has Attached units.

Revise:
- Fold Attached units before the dead-extra test.
- Collapse a combo to its top-value target instead of dropping it, so the post-roll fallback stays scored.
- Move CH-OVERKILL to its own parameter, default 0.
- Bench CH-EXTRA alone.

Changed declarations: about 7-10 per game in the Custodes mirror and asym, about 1-2 in the Orks mirror.

issues.situation: CH-EXTRA drops a combo when it should strip the dead extra. In _evaluate_multi_target_charge, `continue` skips every combo that has a dead extra. Take a combo whose dead extra is the NEAR target and whose top is the FAR target. Its EV is p(rolls that reach only the near target) x v_near + p_far x v_far. The design's own root cause says this is exactly what declaring the far target alone earns, because the post-roll re-pick falls back to the near target. But a single declaration is scored p x v with no fallback credit. Once the combo is gone, the AI compares p_near*v_near with p_far*v_far and often declares the near, lower-value target alone. _select_post_roll_charge_targets then keeps that target on every roll, so the valuable target is never taken. The base did take it on high rolls. Bench example (Custodes mirror, code formulas, bench stats): a Custodian Guard charger has an enemy CG 4.5" away (need 5, value_if about 20.3; it hits back 13.9 dmg, x2 = 27.8, so it is a dead extra) and an enemy Blade Champion 7" away (need 7, capped value_if about 26.2). The base declares [CG+BC], EV about 20.4. The fix declares [CG] alone (16.9 vs 15.3). By the same model, [BC] alone would be worth 20.4. The drop also takes the fallback credit out of the unit's best score, which shifts the cross-unit declaration order. This path is most of the design's bench reach.
issues.proposed_change: Do not `continue`. When every non-top member of a combo is a dead extra, re-emit the combo as DECLARE_CHARGE at the top target only and keep combo_result.score: the EV already floors dead extras at 0 and books the post-roll fallback. Have _score_multi_target_combo return the top's target_id and name (e.g. result.ct_top) for this. A triple that still has live extras can still be dropped, because its live pair is scored on its own anyway. All 3 decision checks keep their outcome: s7480 -> [Blade Champion Alpha] at EV about 29.0 (it beats [remnant] at 21.6); s7461 -> [Beastboss]; s7465 P1 -> [Beastboss]. Add a test with a near dead extra and a far top where p_near*v_near > p_far*v_far: with the fix on, the AI must declare the far target.

issues.situation: CH-EXTRA splits Attached units. A bodyguard and its leader are separate unit ids, and the base reaches both ids through a T7-50 combo (e.g. replay log: 'Battlewagon Beta declares a charge at Blade Champion Alpha + Custodian Guard Sodality Delta'). The leader (or the bodyguard) hits back, so CH-EXTRA marks it a dead extra and drops the combo, and the AI declares only one id. ChargePhase._validate_engagement_range_constraints and _compute_charge_move (constraint 4) then treat the other component as a non-target enemy. The charge move must therefore stay more than 2" from a model that stands in coherency with the target, so the move is awkward or fails after a successful roll (SKIP_CHARGE). The designer's own replay shows this: s7480 r3 P1, CG Delta [CG Beta + Blade Champion Gamma] -> [CG Beta]. In that save U_BLADE_CHAMPION_C_P2 has attached_to = U_CUSTODIAN_GUARD_B_P2. Under 11e 19.01 the leader is part of the unit and fights back anyway, so the reason 'the extra only keeps the charger locked and hit' does not apply. This never happens in the bench (no attached units), but it does in real games.
issues.proposed_change: In the dead-extra check, never mark a member that belongs to the same Attached unit as another combo member: compare _attached_unit_target_id(id), or use RulesEngine.attached_unit_component_ids. A bodyguard and its leader are then kept or dropped together. Add a test with an attached leader: the declaration must list both ids.

issues.situation: test_extra_target_that_adds_nothing does not test anything. The boyz are north and the boss is south of a 1-model Battlewagon, about 10.3" apart edge to edge; the spread limit for a 1-model charger is 3.57" + 3.15" = 6.7". _score_multi_target_combo therefore returns -INF at the feasibility check, before CH-EXTRA runs, so the test also passes on base (tg.size() <= 1 also passes on a SKIP_CHARGE). Test 1 does pin both parts: with the cap only, [remnant, champ] has EV about 33.3, above 28.8; with CH-EXTRA only, the remnant stays top and the champ is a live extra. So the file still fails on base for the right reason. Test 2 compares _ai_description, and that text does not include the score.
issues.proposed_change: Put the boss within about 6" of the boyz so the pair is feasible. Assert that the combo is declared with FIX_CHARGE_TARGET=0 and that a single target is declared with 1. In test 2, compare the score (e.g. charge_eval or the 'Best charge' score), not only the description.

issues.situation: The CH-OVERKILL gate (ct_cap) is set per charger, which makes the cross-unit comparison inconsistent. A charger with 2+ targets above 3% is scored with capped damage; a charger with one target is scored with uncapped damage. A second target at a 3% chance, or a worthless one that scores 0, is enough to switch the cap on. _evaluate_best_charge then ranks units against each other, and against the bar, on these mixed scales. Example from the Custodes mirror: two units can reach the same 6-W Blade Champion. For the unit that has a second option the BC scores about 26; for the other unit it scores about 47. So the declaration order changes for reasons that have nothing to do with value.
issues.proposed_change: Either cap for every charger and accept the rare change at the bar, or use the capped score only to pick the target inside the unit and carry that target's uncapped score into unit_best, best_score and the bar. With the second option, the unit order and the charge/no-charge call stay as in base.

issues.situation: The post-roll re-pick is still uncapped. _select_post_roll_charge_targets calls _score_charge_target with cap_overkill=false. The fix moves declarations toward farther, more valuable targets. When the roll misses such a target and 2+ targets are selectable, the re-pick still prefers the overkill remnant.
issues.proposed_change: Behind the same param, pass cap_overkill = (FIX_CHARGE_TARGET > 0 and scored.size() >= 2) in the re-pick.

issues.situation: Cost, style and logging. The ct_eligible pre-pass computes _get_closest_model_pair_info and _estimate_charge_terrain_penalty a second time for every (charger, target), repeating the work of the main loop. dead_extra is computed ungated in _score_multi_target_combo; this is harmless, because the key is unused at param 0. CH-EXTRA prints one line per skipped combo per evaluation (118-314 lines per game in the Custodes pair). Keeping those lines is fine, but they are what inflates bench_fires_per_game.
issues.proposed_change: Optional: compute need and prob for every target in one first pass and use the same values for both the gate and the scoring.

issues.situation: For an Attached unit, the cap uses the wrong wounds. CH-OVERKILL caps at _calculate_kill_threshold of the target id only. When the target is the bodyguard id of an Attached unit, damage beyond the bodyguard's wounds goes on to the leader under 11e, so the cap undervalues a charge at a damaged bodyguard that has a healthy leader. This does not happen in the bench.
issues.proposed_change: Cap at the total remaining wounds of all attached_unit_component_ids.

reviews.fires_in_bench:
My estimate: about 2-3 changed charge declarations (target sets) per game, pooled, in the candidate seat. By fixture: Custodes mirror about 3.5-4.5, Custodes vs Orks about 2-3, Orks mirror about 0.5-1. The designer's 245 lines/game count evaluation logs, not decisions: each CH-EXTRA line is one combo skipped in one evaluation, and each CH-OVERKILL line is one capped (charger, target) score. That overstates changed decisions by roughly 50-100x. The figures come from the code's trigger conditions:
(1) CH-EXTRA can change a declaration only where the base would declare a multi-target charge. The V10 reach run counted 16 / 18 / 3 'targets picked after the roll' GameEventLog lines per game (cus / asy / ork, both seats). The replay debug logs show 2 such lines per declaration (the 'Thinking:' header and the action entry). That gives about 4 / 4.5 / 0.75 multi-target declarations per game in one seat. In the Custodes mirror every unit except the Prosecutors hits back for more than 0.2x its value (a Custodian Guard hits a Custodian Guard charger for about 13.9 dmg, x2 = 27.8), so nearly all of those combos are dropped. In asym, Custodes chargers often keep live Ork extras (Gretchin, Mek, Warbikers, Stormboyz), while Ork combos into Custodes are dropped. The Orks mirror has few combos.
(2) CH-OVERKILL needs a charger with 2+ targets that can overkill one of them: 5-model Custodes into a 6-W Blade Champion, 4-W Prosecutors or damaged units; Deffkoptas, Stompa or Wartrike into Gretchin, Mek or characters. It re-ranks targets, or the unit order, about 0.3-1 time per game. Kill bonuses survive the cap, so a capped Blade Champion still usually beats a full Custodian Guard.
It clears the 1.0/game reach gate, but it is a broad change: it rescores every evaluation of a charger with 2+ targets and removes nearly all multi-target declarations. Judge it as a full-game-safety change. The attached-unit part never fires in the bench.
reviews.strengths:
CH-OVERKILL is a principled valuation fix. ch_damage was credited beyond the target's remaining wounds and then scaled up by the short-charge multipliers. Only that term is capped; the can_halve / can_wipe kill bonuses, retaliation and coordination still use the real estimate, so nothing is double counted. The design also spots a real defect in the combo scorer: with a dead extra, the combo EV equals the single-target score, so the base declared such combos only on floating-point rounding (s7461 [Beast Snagga Boyz (value 0) + Beastboss], s7480 [remnant + Allarus #2]). CH-EXTRA settles those ties toward not engaging an extra unit that only hits back.
The s7480 decision check agrees with the code: capped, the remnant's value_if is about 22.2, and its lock-down share of 4.44 is below its 5.0 hit-back, so it is a dead extra (by a narrow 0.56). Blade Champion Alpha at 25.9 beats the remnant at 21.6.
FIX_CHARGE_TARGET=0 restores the base exactly: ct_cap is computed only when the param is above 0, the combo is never dropped, and the ungated dead_extra key is unused. The existing direct test of the combo scorer is untouched, debug logs are only added, the guardrails and lone-target charge/no-charge calls are unchanged, and no unit is held back.
Test 1 drives the real _decide_charge path. It fails on base for the right reason (the base declares [remnant, champ], EV about 47.6), it needs both parts (it still fails with either part alone), and it sets and erases the override. The report is candid: the s7465 P1 change is not the 'no charge' alternative, and it says that CH-EXTRA is broad.
reviews.summary:
The headline finding is handled correctly. At s7480, CH-OVERKILL plus CH-EXTRA turn [remnant + Allarus #2] into [Blade Champion Alpha], which matches the +5.75 alternative, and s7461 gets its alternative too. Parameter 0 restores the base exactly.
Most of the bench reach comes from CH-EXTRA, and that part has two real bugs.
1. It drops a dead-extra combo instead of re-declaring the combo's top target at the combo's EV. The design itself says the post-roll re-pick gives a single declaration its fallback target, but a single declaration is scored without that fallback. So when the near target is the dead extra, the AI often switches to declaring the near, lower-value target alone and never takes the valuable one, which works against the cluster's own goal.
2. It splits Attached units (bodyguard + leader ids) into single-id declarations. The engine's per-id non-target engagement check then constrains the charge move or fails it. This shows in the designer's own s7480 P1 replay; it does not happen in the bench.
Both have small, concrete fixes, and neither fix changes the 3 decision checks. The third test does not test anything because its combo is geometrically infeasible, but test 1 still pins both parts. The design is a broad change in the bench: about 2-3 changed declarations per game, mostly in the fixtures with Custodes. Verdict: revise, then bench.

scores.note: Exact flip at s7480 r3 P2: Blade Champion Alpha alone, which is the measured +5.75 alternative. The designer's own forced replay backs each leg: the cap alone gave 'remnant + Blade Champion', which played identically to base (E 0.00, n12), so CT-COMBO is needed. All 4 cluster guardrails are unchanged. The test fails on base (3 of 8) through _decide_charge, and the code is the smallest and exactly gated. Problems: (1) The 2x gate is not a remnant test with bench datasheets. 25 spear attacks give 13.89 expected damage, which is 2.31x a full 6-W Blade Champion; it also trips on full Prosecutors and on small Ork units in asym. (2) It ignores kill cards. From the logged record, s7431 r3 P1 (harmful -5.00) has a 13.725 tie between the 1-W Blade Champion Alpha and the 7-W Blade Champion Gamma. The cap drops Alpha to about 5.49, so the AI switches to Gamma, which is an attached leader. Reach: 45.5 log lines per game (Custodes mirror only). As written, about 1-6 changed declarations per game; about 0.5-2 after the required gates.

CT-FALLBACK has the soundest idea: it gives single declarations their 11e post-roll value. But at s7480 the fix declares Allarus #2 at 9+, not the measured alternative; its own choice measured +4.58 [-1.29, 10.46] n12. The decision test passes on CT-CAP alone, so the fallback is pinned only through the helper. The Command Re-roll check still measures the needed roll from the declared far target, so the AI spends 1 CP re-rolling rolls the fallback already counts. In the reserve-free bench nothing blocks this re-roll: FURY OF THE EMPEROR needs an ingress move (CustodesCodexOther._check, arrived_from_reserves). CT-CAP caps at any ratio, including a Blade Champion at 10 dmg vs 7 W, and it flips s7431 r3 (5.49 vs 10.98). It rescores most charge evaluations, so it is a broad change: 104 lines per game, about 1-5 changed declarations.

Exact flips at s7480 and at the neutral s7461. CH-EXTRA is the broadest change of the three. It removes nearly every multi-target declaration (about 6-7 changed declarations per game in the Custodes fixtures). It drops a combo instead of collapsing it to the top target, so the valuable target can be lost. In real games it splits leader + bodyguard pairs: the designer's own s7480 P1 replay shows it. Six measured split alternatives, where I verified the attachments in the saves (s7412, s7434, s7442, s7458, s7472, s7475), average -1.33 VP, all neutral. The bench cannot see this harm. Test 3 is geometrically infeasible (10.3" vs a 6.7" spread), so it passes on base. The ct_cap pre-pass repeats the pair-info and terrain work. CH-OVERKILL also flips s7431 r3. 245 log lines per game.

verdict.reasons:
Narrow wins only if the required changes below are made. As submitted, none of the three designs is safe.

Why narrow:
(1) It reproduces the clear finding exactly: at s7480 r3 P2 the Allarus charge Blade Champion Alpha alone, which is the measured +5.75 [1.46, 10.04] n24 alternative. Each of its two legs has its own replay evidence. With the cap alone the AI declared 'remnant + Blade Champion', and those games were identical to base (E 0.00, n12). In the decoded save that pair is 8.72" apart edge to edge. The combo spread check accepted it, but the charge move cannot engage both.
(2) It has the smallest surface. Parameter 0 restores the base exactly, and the failing-first test drives _decide_charge. All three patches apply cleanly to 12e0753 (I checked in a scratch copy).
(3) The runners-up carry larger unmeasured changes:
- Root's own choice at f1 is not the measured alternative (A#2, CI crosses 0). Its fallback scoring conflicts with the charge re-roll logic: FURY OF THE EMPEROR requires an ingress move, so in the reserve-free bench nothing stops a 1-CP Command Re-roll of rolls the fallback already counts.
- Game's CH-EXTRA rewrites almost every multi-target declaration and drops a combo instead of collapsing it. In real games it splits Attached units; the measured split alternatives lean negative (mean -1.33 over 6 positions).

Defects I verified that all three designs share:
(a) The cap fires on full-health targets in the bench rosters. A 5-model Custodian Guard does 13.89 expected damage against a full 6-W Blade Champion. Narrow caps from 2x up; root and game cap whenever damage exceeds the wounds left.
(b) s7431 r3 P1 is measured harmful (-5.00, n12) and is a section-8 guard. From the logged decision record:
- Blade Champion Alpha (1 W) and Gamma (7 W) tie at 13.725.
- Narrow caps Alpha to about 5.49; root and game cap both (5.49 vs 10.98).
- So every design switches the Allarus to Gamma. Gamma is a leader standing 0.37" from its bodyguard and 0.43" from Alpha, so the charge loses the near-certain kill (Assassination + Overwhelming Force + destroyed-on-objective, about +11 VP) and may fail outright.
- Nobody replayed this; it comes from the scores.
- A CHARACTER or kill-card exemption restores the base tie there. It keeps the s7480 flip, because the remnant is not a CHARACTER. P2's cards at s7480 are Assassination, Secure No Man's Land and A Tempting Target.
(c) The bench_fires numbers (45.5 / 104 / 245) are log lines from the Custodes mirror only, not changed decisions. As written, narrow changes about 1-6 declarations per game. After the gates below, the estimate is about 0.5-2. Its own effect will be too small for the bench to resolve, so it will be measured mainly as part of the round-5 bundle.

Caveat on the finding itself: the alternative kills a CHARACTER while P2 holds Assassination. P2's Blade Champion C is in base contact with that target (0.012"), and it carries flags.in_engagement but not is_engaged, which only FightPhase sets. So the FOCUS-CHARGE bonus never fired. Part of the +5.75 may therefore be mission and focus value that the overkill cap does not model.
required_changes: Depletion gate on both arms. Apply CT-OVERKILL (_score_charge_target) and the ct_overkill flag (_evaluate_best_charge) only when ct_hp <= 0.5 x the target's starting wounds. Starting wounds = the sum of each model's 'wounds' over all models, dead ones included. Keep the 2x ratio. Put the test in one shared helper so the two call sites cannot disagree. Add a unit test: a 5-model bench Custodian Guard (13.89 expected damage) against a full 6-W Blade Champion and against full 4-model Prosecutors. ch_damage must stay uncapped and the declaration must match FIX_CHARGE_TARGET=0.

Kill-value exemption. Skip both arms when the target is a CHARACTER, or when destroying it pays one of the decider's own active kill cards, read from _get_secondary_awareness(player). This covers: a kill_keywords match; the unit id in marked_targets; kill_big_units_min met; kill_near_objectives with the target within OBJECTIVE_CONTROL_RANGE_PX of an objective. Without it, s7431 r3 P1 (harmful -5.00) switches from the 1-W Blade Champion Alpha to the attached 7-W Blade Champion Gamma.

Attached units (they occur in real games; the bench fixtures have none). Compute ct_hp and starting wounds over the whole Attached unit. Map ids with the AI-side _attached_unit_target_id and walk both linkage sides, because RulesEngine cannot be referenced from AIDecisionMaker in --script mode. Never let CT-COMBO remove a combo member that belongs to the same Attached unit as another member.

Restrict CT-COMBO to targets the charger cannot engage together. Keep a gated target in the combo when any of its models is within engagement range (2") of another combo target. Otherwise the single declaration's move must stay more than 2" from that target as a non-target (_compute_charge_move constraint 4), and it can fail after a successful roll.

Log at decision level for the reach gate. In _evaluate_best_charge, also compute the pick with the fix's adjustments off; the uncapped values are already available. Print one '[CHARGE_TARGET] changed: <unit> <old ids> -> <new ids>' line only when the declaration differs. Keep the existing per-evaluation lines. Report changed declarations per game per fixture (cus / asy / ork) next to the V2-1 line count.

Real-save guard tests with the r4 root .w40ksave harness. s7480 r3 P2 must declare [U_BLADE_CHAMPION_A]. s7431 r3 P1 must still declare [U_BLADE_CHAMPION_A_P2]. s7403 r3 P1, s7466 r3 P2, s7465 r2 P2, s7470 r2 P2 (_1 and _2), s7480 r3 P1 and s7467 r2 P1 must keep their logged declarations.
